content.title: About
content.content: Pepper steak is a dish of thinly sliced beef quickly stir‑fried with bell peppers, onion and soy sauce. It is popular in Asian cuisine, especially Chinese and Thai, and is often served over rice or noodles.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The dish appeared in the United States in the mid‑20th century as an adaptation of Chinese "chow fan".
Traditionally tender cuts such as sirloin or tenderloin are used so the meat stays juicy during fast cooking.
The sweet soy sauce combined with spicy pepper creates a characteristic sweet‑savory balance.
Variations may include carrots, mushrooms, pineapple or toasted cashews.
High‑heat cooking preserves the crisp texture of the vegetables.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Beef provides a complete source of protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Iron from beef supports hemoglobin formation and helps prevent anemia.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The dish supplies B12, B6 and niacin, which are important for nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Antioxidants from peppers
items.content: Bell peppers are rich in vitamin C and carotenoids that combat oxidative stress.

items.title: Low in carbs
items.content: With vegetables as the main carbohydrate source, pepper steak fits well into low‑carb diets.

items.title: Beef allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to beef.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Soy sauce adds a lot of salt; people with hypertension should limit the amount.

items.title: Overcooking
items.content: Cooking the meat too long can make it tough and generate harmful compounds.

items.title: Foodborne illness
items.content: Undercooked beef may contain pathogens such as E. coli.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Slice beef thinly, marinate in soy sauce, ginger and garlic for 15‑30 minutes. Stir‑fry quickly over high heat with sliced bell peppers and onion, then add a sauce made from soy sauce, sugar and cornstarch. Serve hot over rice or noodles.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Fresh beef should be kept in the refrigerator for up to 2 days, while the cooked dish can be stored in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Marinated beef can be frozen for up to 3 months.
